$NVDA today announces capacity agreements with substrate, packaging, testing and optical engine suppliers.

- Substrate agreements with Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron to expand by 2.5x
- $AMKR to increase advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028, with a new $1.3B agreement
- Multibillion dollar capacity reservation advance to support Ibiden's plant in Japan
- "By 2028, production allocated to $NVDA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics' total annual package substrate production capacity"
- KYEC with $1.1B capacity reservation in advance
- SPIL for optical engine capacity for CPO by 15x by H2 2027 and double that for 2028

Well, that's a lot of news. As Jensen Huang puts it: "Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint."

I didn't predict and do not predict defense running ahead of offense automatically. I predict cybersecurity will be endgame defense-favoring but the transition will be hard. In particular, "good guys find vulns in already-released software before the bad guys do" is not a defense-favoring game. Making the game defense-favoring requires deeper shifts in methodology including formal verification, aggressive TCB minimization, etc, and we've only barely started making those transitions.

(This distinction is a big reason why I continue to be friendly toward slowdowns/pauses, and we need >1% of GDP going toward cyber + bio + physical world hardening)
